---

## Synthesis Overview

This PR replaces the multi-format YAML-frontmatter savepoint storage with a clean extension-based dispatch scheme (strings → `.md`, structured data → `.json`), adds `list` / `list-full` operations, extracts a shared `_run.ts` subprocess helper, and introduces `_validate_step` path-traversal guards at the tool boundary. The three models agreed substantially on the core structural and security findings, but diverged on severity ratings and each model surfaced at least one finding the others missed.

The highest-confidence finding — `list_savepoint_names()` absent from the abstract repository interface — was flagged by all three models (though with differing severity). A confirmed write-path correctness bug (stale sibling extension when overwriting a savepoint with a different data type) was found exclusively by GPT but verified by direct code inspection; it should be treated as a fix requirement despite its singular classification. The async generator defect in `asyncio.to_thread` calls was independently identified by two of three models.

**Model Agreement Score:** 6/10 — The models converged on the same root issues but disagreed on severity assignments and each missed one or two findings that others caught.

## Consensus Findings

### ★★★ Unanimous Findings (All Three Models Agree)

```
[U-W-01] list_savepoint_names() absent from SavepointRepository abstract interface
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness / Architecture
File: src/domain/repositories/savepoint_repository.py
Lines: 1–50 (interface definition)
Detail: list_savepoint_names() is implemented on FilesystemSavepointRepository and
called directly by savepoint_manager.py, but is not declared as an @abstractmethod
on SavepointRepository. The gap is harmless today because savepoint_manager.py
constructs the concrete class directly. However, this violates the Dependency
Inversion Principle: any alternative implementation of SavepointRepository
(mock, test double, future adapter) is not contractually required to provide the
method, and mypy will reject calls typed against the abstract class at the call site.
Claude rated this Warning; GPT rated it Suggestion; Gemini rated it Critical. The
consensus is Warning — it is not a runtime defect today but is a meaningful interface
incompleteness that creates a latent trap.
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✓  Gemini ✓
Suggestion: Add the declaration between list_savepoints and clear_all_savepoints in
savepoint_repository.py:
  @abstractmethod
  async def list_savepoint_names(self) -> list[str]: ...
```

---

### ★★☆ Majority Findings (Two of Three Models Agree)

```
[M-W-01] asyncio.to_thread(rglob, pattern) returns a lazy generator; I/O still executes on the main thread
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness / Performance
File: src/infrastructure/storage/savepoint_repository.py
Lines: ~138–143 (list_savepoint_names), ~173–178 (clear_all_savepoints), ~182–186 (clear_all_savepoints rglob "*")
Detail: asyncio.to_thread(self._current_story_dir.rglob, pattern) runs Path.rglob()
in a worker thread and returns the resulting generator object. The generator is lazy —
no filesystem I/O occurs during creation. All directory traversal happens when the
returned generator is iterated in the for-loop body, which runs on the main event-loop
thread. The offloading is therefore a no-op for all three affected callsites:
list_savepoint_names (two rglob calls), list_savepoints (delegates to
list_savepoint_names), and clear_all_savepoints (three rglob calls). In the current
CLI context there is no competing event-loop work, so this is latent rather than
immediately observable. Embedding this class in any async service would produce
event-loop blocking under load. Claude rated this Warning; Gemini rated it Critical.
The consensus is Warning given the CLI-only deployment context, but the fix is trivial.
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✗  Gemini ✓
Dissenting view: GPT did not identify this finding. The two-model consensus and
direct code verification confirm it is genuine.
Suggestion: Materialise the generator inside the thread:
  await asyncio.to_thread(lambda: list(self._current_story_dir.rglob(pattern)))
Apply the same lambda pattern to all three rglob call sites in clear_all_savepoints.
```

```
[M-W-02] No migration path documented for savepoints created under the previous format
Severity: Warning
Category: Documentation / Operational Risk
File: docs/manual.md (general); src/infrastructure/storage/savepoint_repository.py
Lines: general
Detail: The PR removes all YAML-frontmatter parsing branches. Savepoints written under
the old multi-format scheme (YAML frontmatter containing structured data fields) will
now be read by load_savepoint() as raw strings — the literal frontmatter text — rather
than as a parsed Python dict or list. Any active story whose pipeline depends on a
saved structured savepoint (outline, characters, etc.) will receive unexpected string
data and may fail with a JSONDecodeError or AttributeError downstream, depending on
how the caller uses the loaded value. The research file and PR description acknowledge
the format change but provide no migration instruction. Claude rated this Suggestion;
GPT rated it Warning. The consensus is Warning given the real operational risk to
active stories.
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✓  Gemini ✗
Dissenting view: Gemini did not report this. The finding is confirmed by the removal
of the compatibility read branches in load_savepoint() and the absence of any migration
tooling in the diff.
Suggestion: Add a migration note to docs/manual.md (or a separate migration guide)
documenting: (1) that structured savepoints from before this change must be cleared
before resuming a pipeline, (2) that savepoint-mgr clear followed by re-running the
affected steps is the supported path, and (3) that string-body .md savepoints are
forward-compatible with no action required.
```

### ★☆☆ Singular Findings (Only One Model Reported)

> **Note on [S-C-01]:** Despite being reported by only one model, this finding was
> independently verified by direct code inspection. It should be treated as a required
> fix rather than a low-confidence suggestion.

```
[S-C-01] ⚠ CODE-VERIFIED ⚠  Overwriting a savepoint with a different data type leaves a stale sibling file
Severity: Critical (code-verified)
Category: Correctness
File: src/infrastructure/storage/savepoint_repository.py
Lines: 55–67 (save_savepoint), 69–84 (load_savepoint)
Detail: save_savepoint() dispatches on isinstance(data, str): strings go to
<base>.md, non-strings go to <base>.json. It never deletes the file with the
other extension. load_savepoint() always checks <base>.json first, then falls
through to <base>.md. Consequence: if a pipeline step previously saved structured
data (creating step.json) and is later re-run saving a string (creating step.md),
both files now exist on disk. All subsequent loads will return the stale JSON
payload instead of the new string — silent state corruption with no error surfaced.
The inverse case (JSON overwriting a previous string) leaves an orphaned .md
file; list_savepoint_names() deduplicates by stem so the file stays hidden but
consumes disk space.
Claude noted "JSON precedence when both extensions coexist" is tested (Phase 5),
which confirms the load priority ordering is correct, but the test covers
intentional coexistence rather than the accidental coexistence created by a
type-change overwrite. Gemini reviewed the same file and did not flag the write
path. This is verified genuine.
Model: GPT ✓
Assessment: Confirmed genuine. The write path definitively does not clear the
sibling. The load path definitively checks JSON first. The resulting stale-data
scenario is reproducible and produces incorrect pipeline outputs.
Suggestion: At the start of save_savepoint(), delete the sibling path before
writing the new one:
  base = self._get_savepoint_base(step_name)
  # Remove stale sibling to prevent type-mismatch on load
  sibling = base.with_suffix(".md" if not isinstance(data, str) else ".json")
  await asyncio.to_thread(sibling.unlink, missing_ok=True)  # Python 3.8+
Then proceed with the existing write logic. Add a regression test: save a step
as JSON, then save the same step as a string, and assert that the subsequent
load returns the string.
```

```
[S-W-01] FilesystemSavepointRepository._get_savepoint_base lacks path-traversal validation
Severity: Warning
Category: Security / Defense-in-Depth
File: src/infrastructure/storage/savepoint_repository.py
Lines: 26–53
Detail: _get_savepoint_base() handles step names containing "/" by splitting on the
separator and joining path components, but performs no ".." component check and no
resolve() / is_relative_to() guard. A caller that constructs the repository directly
(unit test, future service, DI container) and passes a step name such as
"../../etc/passwd" will silently escape _current_story_dir. The tool layer's
_validate_step() closes the real attack surface for the current CLI entry point,
but the repository itself is not safe as a reusable component.
Model: Claude ✓
Assessment: Genuine defense-in-depth finding. The current attack surface is closed
by the tool layer. Worth fixing to make the repository class safe in isolation.
Suggestion: At the top of _get_savepoint_base(), add:
  resolved = (self._current_story_dir / step_name).resolve()
  if not resolved.is_relative_to(self._current_story_dir.resolve()):
      raise StorageError(f"Step name escapes story directory: {step_name}")
```

[S-S-03] Missing return type hint on list_savepoints override
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Style

Lines: ~133
Detail: The overriding implementation of list_savepoints() drops the return type

Model: Gemini ✓

```
[S-S-04] TOCTOU race in delete_savepoint (path.exists() + path.unlink())
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Correctness
File: src/infrastructure/storage/savepoint_repository.py
Lines: ~118–120
Detail: delete_savepoint() checks path.exists() then calls path.unlink() in two
separate asyncio.to_thread calls. Between the two dispatches, another coroutine
could delete the file, causing the unlink() to raise FileNotFoundError. Python
3.8+ path.unlink(missing_ok=True) handles this atomically in a single dispatch.
Model: Gemini ✓
Assessment: Genuine correctness point. The race is theoretical in the CLI context
but the single-call form is both more correct and more efficient.
Suggestion: Replace the exists()+unlink() pattern with:
  await asyncio.to_thread(path.unlink, missing_ok=True)
```

```
[S-S-05] set_story_directory parameter named prompt_filename rather than story_name
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Style
File: src/domain/repositories/savepoint_repository.py
Lines: ~10
Detail: The abstract method set_story_directory(self, prompt_filename: str) accepts
a filename from which the concrete implementation derives the story_name via
Path(prompt_filename).stem. The interface parameter name leaks an input-layer
concept (prompt file path) into the domain interface, creating a tight coupling to
the prompt-based invocation model.
Model: Gemini ✓
Assessment: Genuine style concern. Low urgency — a rename would require updating
all callers. Only worth addressing in a follow-up refactor, not as a blocker.
Suggestion: Rename to story_name: str in both the ABC and concrete class, and
adjust callers to pass Path(prompt_filename).stem directly.
```

## Overall Assessment

**Not ready for merge as-is.** The extension-based dispatch design is sound and the `_run.ts` extraction and security guards at the tool layer are genuinely good work. However, four issues require resolution:

1. The write path in `save_savepoint()` does not clean up a stale sibling file on type change, causing silent data corruption on overwrite — this is a real correctness defect (verified).
2. `list_savepoint_names()` is missing from the abstract interface — this is a DIP violation and a contract gap agreed on by all three models.
3. The `asyncio.to_thread(rglob, ...)` calls return lazy generators that are then iterated on the main thread — a latent async defect with a trivial fix.
4. There is no migration path or documentation for active stories with pre-existing structured savepoints, which represent a real operational risk on deploy.

Items 1–4 should be addressed before merge. Items 5–10 are optional improvements.
